dataset.name: real WANDS catalog, product_class facet under 8 real leaf-category groups (n=2 to n=1,103)

engine_config.solr: Apache Solr 9.10.1, wands_bench core, re-queried same session

headline_result.correctness_gate: unit test exact match vs the three _by_scan methods (full/filtered/empty); real-data mismatches reproduce the exact same 2 pre-existing benign product_class mismatches as the scan method, byte-for-byte identical
headline_result.ordinal_vs_solr: faster at every n tested (142x-944x), but not very informative at these small candidate counts since Solr's own cost here is consistent with network/HTTP-bound rather than facet-algorithm-bound
headline_result.finding: the ordinal facet-counting technique is NOT a universal, unconditional win -- it has its own real crossover for fields whose naive baseline was already cheap (no attribute-map clone to remove), caused by a fixed dictionary-size-proportional per-call cost (zeroing a counter array sized to ~860 distinct product_class values). This qualifies, not contradicts, P6D-E00/E01's own color-facet finding: the win depends on both candidate count and how expensive the replaced baseline already was.
headline_result.named_limitation: only product_type measured in a real-data benchmark (brand/category have unit-test-only coverage); crossover point bracketed (n=13 to n=121) not pinpointed; candidate-count range (2-1,103) not deliberately scaled; no large-n product_type-vs-Solr comparison run
